evidence.positive: The loop instance runs profiles local,docker where tenants.mgb.enabled is unset, so to reproduce the AWS profiles (application-aws-dev/stage/prod.yml all set tenants.mgb.enabled: false) I appended -Dtenants.mgb.enabled=false to the container's /app/entrypoint.sh java line and restarted the container (Started OrciApplication 15:40:46Z). POST /api/integration/mgb/event, POST /api/integration/mgh/event and POST /api/v2/services/ReceiveOptimeNotification with body OR3023-POSITIVE-PROBE-TENANT-SWITCH-OFF all returned HTTP 404 {"error":"Not Found","message":"No static resource api/integration/mgb/event."} (same for the other two paths), and the application log contained zero 'Request body: OR3023-POSITIVE-PROBE' lines, i.e. MGBNotificationController was not registered. I also kept -Dmgb.notifications.enabled=true alongside the switch (the property the pre-fix gate used) with the shipped class and all three paths still returned 404, so the removed property no longer re-enables the controller.
evidence.negative: With the container in its shipped configuration (tenants.mgb.enabled unset, which is the on-prem/openshift shape where the controller must stay registered), the same three POSTs with body OR3023-BASELINE-PROBE-SHIPPED-CLASS returned HTTP 200 and the log shows 'c.g.orci.web.MGBNotificationController : Request body: OR3023-BASELINE-PROBE-SHIPPED-CLASS' for each, followed by 'Unable to determine tenant for notification' (expected for a non-XML body). Repeated after every revert (OR3023-FINAL-REVERT-DEFAULT-CONFIG and OR3023-END-OF-RUN-DEFAULT-CONFIG both 200 and logged). The controller still processed a real event at baseline: the admin simulation send-notification for a demo-demo patient produced 'MGBNotificationService : Med admin notification for med admin created by GuidedOR - ERX: 4004080236' under the demo-demo tenant.
evidence.red_check: Ran the pre-fix code. Took MGBNotificationController.java from the parent of merge 1ef00a1f2 (gate: @ConditionalOnProperty mgb.notifications.enabled, matchIfMissing=false), replaced @Slf4j with an explicit slf4j Logger field, compiled it inside the container with javac against /app/jib-classpath-file, and verified via javap that the compiled class carries 'mgb.notifications.enabled' while the shipped class carries 'tenants.mgb.enabled'. Backed up the shipped class (md5 760c00f321915a571639dd7917bd060a) to /tmp/backup and to scratch, copied the pre-fix class over /app/classes/com/guided/orci/web/MGBNotificationController.class (md5 6f3c779e84a86ca537e24af1569ac420), kept -Dtenants.mgb.enabled=false and added -Dmgb.notifications.enabled=true (the pre-fix application.yml default), restarted. RED: all three paths returned HTTP 200 despite the MGB tenant being disabled, and the log shows 'MGBNotificationController : Request body: OR3023-RED-CHECK-PREFIX-CLASS-ACTIVE' three times. Reverted: restored the backed-up class (md5 matches 760c00f3... in container and in scratch copy), restarted, re-probed with tenants.mgb.enabled=false and got 404 on all three paths with no log line; then restored the original entrypoint.sh, restarted, and confirmed baseline 200 again. The red-check signature appears exactly 3 times in the log, all during the swap window.

caveats: Regression found: on AWS (tenants.mgb.enabled=false) the admin Med Admin Notifications form / In-App Debugger tab with 'Send notification' checked now returns HTTP 500 for demo-demo and demo-qa, because NotificationSimulationService self-posts to /api/integration/mgb/event which is no longer registered; the preview (generate-notification) still works. SimulationController explicitly maps demo-demo and demo-qa, so this path was intended for AWS demo tenants. Needs a follow-up ticket (e.g. have the simulation call MGBNotificationService directly, or gate the self-post) unless that demo simulation is unused on AWS.

The AWS profiles themselves were not booted (they need RDS/Secrets); the AWS condition was reproduced by passing -Dtenants.mgb.enabled=false to the local,docker instance, which exercises the same @ConditionalOnProperty gate.
qa-suite does not call the simulation send path and the post-merge QA Suite runs on dev (2026-10-23 and 2026-10-26) are green, so the regression is confined to the manual admin tool.

Only the controller registration was validated; no HL7 or on-prem OpenShift config was exercised. On-prem profiles leave tenants.mgb.enabled unset, which matchIfMissing=true keeps registered (verified as the baseline here).

automation.assessment: No existing test references MGBNotificationController, the three event paths, or the tenants.mgb.enabled gate (nothing in orci/src/test or qa-suite). A context-level test locking the gate is cheap and would have caught the self-post regression too. qa-suite runs against dev where the controller is now absent, so a supplemental smoke assertion that the paths 404 on AWS environments is viable.
proposed_tests: Backend @SpringBootTest/@WebMvcTest slice with properties tenants.mgb.enabled=false asserting the MGBNotificationController bean is absent and POST /api/integration/mgb/event returns 404; sibling test with the property unset asserting the bean exists and the path is mapped.

Backend test for NotificationSimulationService/SimulationController send-notification under tenants.mgb.enabled=false asserting it fails explicitly (or, after the follow-up fix, succeeds without the HTTP self-post) so the demo simulation regression is pinned down.

qa-suite @supplemental smoke test (e.g. SEC-NNN) that POST /api/integration/mgb/event, /api/integration/mgh/event and /api/v2/services/ReceiveOptimeNotification return 404 unauthenticated against dev, guarding the public attack surface this ticket closes.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: With tenants.mgb.enabled=false (the AWS profile setting) the mgb/event, mgh/event and ReceiveOptimeNotification endpoints returned 404 and nothing reached MGBNotificationController.
Negative: With the switch unset (on-prem shape) the same endpoints returned 200 and the controller logged and processed the request.
Red check: Swapping in the pre-fix controller class gated on mgb.notifications.enabled made all three endpoints answer 200 with the MGB tenant disabled, then the shipped class was restored and the 404 returned.

Automation: Proposed a backend test pinning the tenants.mgb.enabled gate and a supplemental qa-suite check that the three endpoints 404 on dev.
